questions.p: When you grind the marble to powder, e get plenty surface wey the acid fit touch at once. More surface area mean more collision between acid and marble, so e go react fast pass.

questions.q: For a certain reaction, the rate doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature. If the rate of the reaction at 20°C is 0.02 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, what will the rate be at 50°C?
questions.e: The temperature rises by 50 - 20 = 30°C, which is three lots of 10°C. The rate doubles each time, so the overall factor is 2³ = 8. New rate = 0.02 x 8 = 0.16 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.
questions.p: Temperature rise na 30°C, wey be three times of 10°C. Since rate dey double every 10°C, we multiply by 2 three times: 2x2x2 = 8. So new rate be 0.02 x 8 = 0.16 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

questions.q: Excess granulated zinc is added to 50 cm³ of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid in a flask, and the volume of hydrogen gas produced is recorded against time until the reaction stops. Which description best fits the shape of the graph obtained, and the reason for it?
o: The graph is flat at first and then rises sharply near the end, because the reaction only starts after the acid is fully consumed
The graph is a straight line through the origin throughout, because zinc is in excess and its amount does not change
The graph falls steadily from a high value to zero, because the volume of gas already collected is used up over time
The graph rises steeply at first, then gradually levels off to a flat plateau, because the acid concentration falls as it is used up, slowing and finally stopping the reaction
questions.e: At the start, acid concentration is highest, so collisions and gas production are fastest, giving a steep rise. As the acid is consumed (zinc is in excess), its concentration drops, the rate slows, and the curve flattens into a plateau when the acid runs out and gas production stops.
questions.p: For start, acid plenty well well, so reaction dey fast and gas dey comot quick, na why the graph rise steep. As time dey go, acid dey finish (zinc still plenty), so rate dey slow small small until the acid finish well well and the graph flat out.

questions.q: In a kinetics experiment for the reaction A + B -> products, three trials gave the following initial rates: Trial 1: [A] = 0.10 mol/dm³, [B] = 0.10 mol/dm³, rate = 0.002 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. Trial 2: [A] = 0.20 mol/dm³, [B] = 0.10 mol/dm³, rate = 0.008 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. Trial 3: [A] = 0.10 mol/dm³, [B] = 0.20 mol/dm³, rate = 0.002 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. What is the overall order of the reaction?
questions.e: Comparing trials 1 and 2, doubling [A] (with [B] fixed) quadruples the rate (0.002 to 0.008), so the order with respect to A is 2 (since 2² = 4). Comparing trials 1 and 3, doubling [B] (with [A] fixed) does not change the rate, so the order with respect to B is 0. Overall order = 2 + 0 = 2.
questions.p: If you compare trial 1 and 2, when [A] double, rate quadruple (0.002 to 0.008), so order for A na 2 (because 2² = 4). If you compare trial 1 and 3, when [B] double, rate no change, so order for B na zero. Total order = 2 + 0 = 2.

questions.q: Consider the reversible reaction for ammonia synthesis: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) <=> 2NH₃(g), Delta H = -92 kJ/mol, carried out in a sealed, rigid vessel at constant temperature. If extra nitrogen gas is suddenly pumped into the vessel, what happens to the position of equilibrium?
o: It shifts to the right, but the yield of ammonia decreases
It remains unchanged because nitrogen does not react
It shifts to the right, producing more ammonia
It shifts to the left, producing more hydrogen
questions.e: Adding more N₂ increases the concentration of a reactant. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts in the direction that uses up the extra N₂, which is the forward (right) direction, producing more NH₃.
questions.p: If you add more N₂, di reaction go try use am finish, so e go shift go di right side wey go make more NH₃ come out.

questions.q: In a 1.0 dm3 sealed container, 1.0 mole of gas A and 1.0 mole of gas B were mixed and allowed to react: A(g) + B(g) <=> C(g) + D(g). At equilibrium, chemical analysis showed that 0.60 mole of C had formed. Calculate the equilibrium constant, Kc, for this reaction.
questions.e: At equilibrium: A = 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4 mol, B = 0.4 mol, C = 0.6 mol, D = 0.6 mol (same volume, so concentration equals mol/dm3). Kc = [C][D]/([A][B]) = (0.6 x 0.6)/(0.4 x 0.4) = 0.36/0.16 = 2.25.
questions.p: At equilibrium, A and B remain 0.4 mol each, C and D become 0.6 mol each (volume na 1 dm3 so mol = concentration). Kc = (0.6 x 0.6) divide by (0.4 x 0.4) = 2.25.

questions.q: The water-gas shift reaction used in industry is represented as: CO(g) + H₂O(g) <=> CO₂(g) + H₂(g), Delta H = -41 kJ/mol. If the operating temperature of the reactor is increased while pressure is kept constant, what happens to the value of the equilibrium constant, Kc?
o: Kc decreases because the forward reaction is exothermic
Kc stays the same since Kc only depends on concentration
Kc increases because the reverse reaction becomes exothermic
Kc increases because more product forms
questions.e: The forward reaction is exothermic (Delta H is negative), so increasing temperature favours the reverse (endothermic) reaction, shifting equilibrium left. This means less product and more reactant at equilibrium, so Kc decreases.
questions.p: Di forward reaction na exothermic, so if you increase temperature, e go favour di reverse reaction wey dey endothermic. Equilibrium go shift go left, so Kc go reduce.

questions.q: Permanent hardness of water, caused mainly by dissolved calcium and magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) salts, can be removed by adding which of the following substances to precipitate the ions as insoluble carbonates?
questions.e: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃) reacts with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions in water to form insoluble CaCO₃ and MgCO₃, which settle out and remove permanent hardness. The other substances either do not react with these ions or would make the water worse.
questions.p: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃) de react wit di Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ wey dey water, e go form CaCO₃ and MgCO₃ wey no dey dissolve, so dem go settle down. Di oda options no fit do dis kain reaction well.

questions.q: The solubility of potassium chloride (KCl) in water at 25°C is 34 g per 100 g of water. What mass of KCl is needed to form a saturated solution with 250 g of water at this same temperature?
questions.e: Solubility is given per 100 g of water, so scale up: 250 g water is 2.5 times 100 g. Multiply 34 g by 2.5 to get 85 g of KCl needed to saturate the solution.
questions.p: Dem talk say 34 g KCl dey dissolve for 100 g water. 250 g water na 2.5 times 100 g, so multiply 34 g by 2.5 to get 85 g.

questions.q: A chemistry teacher in Enugu tested two water samples with the same amount of soap solution. Sample A formed a thick lather almost immediately, while Sample B needed far more soap before any lather appeared and produced a sticky scum on top. Based on this observation, what can be concluded about Sample B?
o: Sample B contains dissolved calcium and/or magnesium salts causing hardness
Sample B is distilled water used for laboratory experiments
Sample B is pure, soft water with no dissolved ions
Sample B contains only dissolved oxygen gas
questions.e: Hard water contains Ca₂+ and/or Mg₂+ ions which react with soap to form an insoluble scum instead of lather. The need for extra soap before lathering, plus the scum formed, are classic signs of hard water caused by these dissolved salts.
questions.p: Hard water get Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ wey de react wit soap make scum instead of lather. Di fact say Sample B need plenty soap before e lather, and e still form scum, show say e get dis kain dissolved salts.

questions.q: Which gas, produced mainly from the burning of fossil fuels in cars and factories, is widely recognized as the chief greenhouse gas responsible for trapping infrared radiation and causing global warming?
questions.e: Carbon(IV) oxide (CO₂) traps heat in the atmosphere, causing the greenhouse effect. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are normal air components that do not trap heat significantly. Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of CO₂, making it the main greenhouse gas of concern.
questions.p: Carbon(IV) oxide (CO₂) na im dey trap heat for atmosphere, na im cause greenhouse effect. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon no dey trap heat like that. Na because people dey burn fossil fuel well-well, dat na why CO₂ dey plenty pass.

questions.q: A sample of 2000 cm³ of polluted air collected near a cement factory in Ewekoro was analysed and found to contain 40 cm³ of carbon(II) oxide gas. What is the percentage by volume of carbon(II) oxide in the air sample?
questions.e: Percentage by volume = (volume of CO / total volume of air) x 100 = (40/2000) x 100 = 2%. This simple ratio shows how small amounts of pollutant can be measured in a large air sample. Always divide the pollutant volume by the total volume before multiplying by 100.
questions.p: Percentage by volume = (volume of CO / total volume of air) x 100 = (40/2000) x 100 = 2%. Na so you go take calculate small pollutant inside big air sample. Just divide the pollutant volume by total volume, den multiply by 100.

questions.q: Industrial activities around Kaduna release two gases that dissolve in rainwater droplets to form dilute acids, leading to acid rain that corrodes metal roofs and damages crops. Which pair of gases is most responsible for this phenomenon?
questions.e: Sulphur(IV) oxide dissolves in water to form sulphurous/sulphuric acid, while nitrogen(IV) oxide forms nitric acid; both lower the pH of rainwater and cause acid rain. Carbon(IV) oxide forms only a weak acid and does not cause the severe corrosive acid rain seen near industries. Methane, nitrogen, ozone and hydrogen do not directly form strong acids with rainwater.
questions.p: Sulphur(IV) oxide and nitrogen(IV) oxide dey mix with water make strong acid wey dey cause acid rain. CO₂ dey form weak acid wey no strong reach to damage roof or crop like dat. Methane, nitrogen, ozone and hydrogen no dey form strong acid with rain water.

questions.q: Chlorine atoms released from the breakdown of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) in the stratosphere destroy ozone molecules through a chain reaction. Which equation correctly represents the first step of this ozone-depletion mechanism?
questions.e: In the accepted mechanism, a chlorine radical attacks ozone, forming chlorine monoxide (ClO) and ordinary oxygen: Cl + O₃ -> ClO + O₂. The ClO then reacts further to regenerate Cl, allowing the chain reaction to continue and destroy many ozone molecules. The other equations either show wrong products or reverse the real reaction, so they are not correct steps.
questions.p: For di real mechanism, chlorine radical dey attack ozone make am turn to chlorine monoxide (ClO) and normal oxygen: Cl + O₃ -> ClO + O₂. Dat ClO go react again make Cl come back, so di chain reaction go continue dey destroy ozone. Di oda equations show wrong product or dem reverse di real reaction, so dem no correct.

questions.q: A student heats zinc granules with dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid in a test tube and collects the gas produced. When a lighted splint is brought near the mouth of the tube, a 'pop' sound is heard. Which gas was produced and confirmed by this test?
questions.e: Hydrogen gas gives a characteristic 'pop' sound when a lighted splint is placed near it, because it burns rapidly in air. Oxygen relights a glowing splint, CO₂ puts out a flame, and chlorine bleaches damp litmus; none of these give a pop sound.
questions.p: Hydrogen gas na the one wey dey give 'pop' sound when you bring fire near am, because e dey burn quick quick for air. Oxygen go relight glowing splint, CO₂ go kill fire, chlorine go bleach litmus paper; na only hydrogen dey pop.

questions.q: In the industrial manufacture of ammonia by the Haber process, nitrogen gas and hydrogen gas are combined at about 450°C and 200 atmospheres in the presence of a catalyst to speed up the reaction. Which substance is used as this catalyst?
questions.e: In the Haber process, finely divided iron (often with small amounts of promoters like K₂O or Al₂O₃) is used as the catalyst to speed up the reaction between N₂ and H₂ to form NH₃. Platinum gauze is used for ammonia oxidation in the Ostwald process, vanadium(V) oxide is used in the Contact process for SO₃ production, and manganese(IV) oxide is used to decompose hydrogen peroxide or potassium chlorate(V).
questions.p: For Haber process, dem dey use finely divided iron as catalyst make N₂ and H₂ fast react to form NH₃. Platinum gauze na for Ostwald process wey dem dey oxidize ammonia, vanadium(V) oxide na for Contact process wey dey make SO₃, and MnO₂ na for decompose hydrogen peroxide or KClO₃.

questions.q: Potassium trioxochlorate(V), KClO₃, decomposes on heating according to the equation: 2KClO₃ -> 2KCl + 3O₂. If 2.0 moles of KClO₃ decompose completely, what volume of oxygen gas is produced at standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.), given that 1 mole of gas occupies 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p.?
questions.e: From the equation, 2 mol KClO₃ produces 3 mol O₂, so 2.0 mol KClO₃ also produces 3.0 mol O₂. Volume of O₂ at s.t.p. = 3.0 mol x 22.4 dm3/mol = 67.2 dm3. The other options come from wrong mole ratios or using only part of the stoichiometry.
questions.p: From the equation, 2 mol KClO₃ dey give 3 mol O₂, so 2.0 mol KClO₃ go give 3.0 mol O₂ too. Volume of O₂ for s.t.p. = 3.0 x 22.4 = 67.2 dm3. Other options na from wrong ratio mistake.

questions.q: When sulphur(IV) oxide gas is passed into acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) solution, the purple colour of the solution fades. What role is sulphur(IV) oxide playing in this reaction?
o: It acts as an oxidising agent and is reduced to sulphur
It acts as a drying agent that removes water from the solution
It acts as a reducing agent and is oxidised to the sulphate(VI) ion
It acts only as a bleaching agent similar to chlorine water
questions.e: Sulphur(IV) oxide is a good reducing agent; it reduces the purple manganate(VII) ion (MnO₄-) to colourless Mn₂+ ion while SO₂ itself is oxidised from the +4 to the +6 oxidation state, forming sulphate(VI) ions. This fading of colour is a standard test for SO₂ and for reducing agents in general.
questions.p: Sulphur(IV) oxide na good reducing agent; e dey reduce the purple MnO₄- ion to colourless Mn₂+, while SO₂ im self dey oxidise from +4 to +6 to become sulphate(VI) ion. Na why the purple colour dey fade, and na common test for reducing agent.

questions.q: In industrial aluminium extraction, pure alumina (Al₂O₃) dissolved in molten cryolite is decomposed by electricity to give the metal. What is this electrolytic process called?
questions.e: The Hall-Heroult process is the electrolytic method used worldwide to extract aluminium from molten alumina dissolved in cryolite. The Bayer process only purifies bauxite to alumina, it does not do the electrolysis.
questions.p: Hall-Heroult process na di one wey dem dey use take electricity break down alumina wey dey melt inside cryolite to give aluminium. Bayer process na just to purify bauxite come alumina, e no do di electrolysis part.

questions.q: During the Hall-Heroult extraction of aluminium, cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is mixed with the alumina before electrolysis begins. What is the main reason for adding cryolite?
o: To lower the melting point of alumina, saving energy
To increase the melting point so the cell stays solid
To oxidise the aluminium ions before discharge
To prevent oxygen gas from forming at the anode
questions.e: Pure alumina melts at about 2050°C, which is very expensive to maintain. Dissolving it in cryolite lowers the melting point to around 950°C, so less energy is needed for electrolysis. Cryolite does not oxidise ions or stop oxygen formation.
questions.p: Pure alumina get very high melting point wey go cost plenty money to maintain. Wen dem mix am wit cryolite, di melting point go come down reach around 950°C, so less energy dem go need. Cryolite no dey oxidise ions or stop oxygen from forming.

questions.q: A current of 2.0 A is passed through a copper(II) sulphate solution using copper electrodes for 32 minutes 10 seconds. Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode. (Cu = 64, 1 Faraday = 96500 C/mol, Cu₂+ + 2e- -> Cu)
questions.e: Time = 32x60+10 = 1930 s, so charge Q = I x t = 2.0 x 1930 = 3860 C. Moles of electrons = 3860/96500 = 0.04 mol. Since Cu₂+ needs 2 electrons, moles Cu = 0.04/2 = 0.02 mol, giving mass = 0.02 x 64 = 1.28 g.
questions.p: Time na 32x60+10 = 1930 seconds, so charge Q = I x t = 2.0 x 1930 = 3860 C. Moles of electron = 3860/96500 = 0.04 mol. Since Cu₂+ need 2 electrons, moles of Cu = 0.04/2 = 0.02 mol, mass go be 0.02 x 64 = 1.28 g.

questions.q: Stainless steel is a well known alloy that resists rusting even when exposed to moist air for a long time. Which two elements, when added to iron, mainly give stainless steel this corrosion-resistant property?
questions.e: Stainless steel is made by adding chromium and nickel to iron. The chromium forms a thin, tough oxide layer on the surface that protects the metal from rusting. Zinc, tin, copper and lead are used in other alloys but not for this corrosion resistance in steel.
questions.p: Stainless steel na wen dem add chromium and nickel to iron. Di chromium go form one thin strong oxide layer for di surface wey go protect di metal from rust. Zinc, tin, copper and lead dey important for oda alloys but no be dem dey give steel dis kain protection.

questions.q: What is the general molecular formula that represents the homologous series of alkanes?
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds between carbon atoms. Each additional carbon adds CH₂, starting from CH₄, giving the formula CnH2n+2.
questions.p: Alkane na saturated hydrocarbon wey get only single bond between di carbon atoms. As you dey add carbon, e dey follow CnH2n+2 pattern, starting from methane CH₄.

questions.q: Butane gas (C₄H₁₀) burns completely in oxygen according to the equation: C₄H₁₀ + 13/2 O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O. What is the minimum number of moles of oxygen gas required to completely combust 0.2 mol of butane?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mol butane needs 13/2 = 6.5 mol oxygen. So 0.2 mol butane needs 0.2 x 6.5 = 1.3 mol oxygen.
questions.p: From di equation, 1 mol butane need 6.5 mol oxygen. So 0.2 mol butane go need 0.2 x 6.5 = 1.3 mol oxygen.

questions.q: Hydrogen bromide gas is passed into propene (CH₃-CH=CH₂) and reacts by electrophilic addition. According to Markovnikov's rule, which product forms as the major product?
questions.e: Markovnikov's rule states that the H atom from HBr attaches to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms already, while Br attaches to the more substituted carbon, forming the more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. This gives 2-bromopropane as the major product, not the primary 1-bromopropane.
questions.p: Markovnikov rule tok say di H from HBr go join di carbon wey get more H already, while Br go join di carbon wey get fewer H, because e dey form stable secondary carbocation. Na why 2-bromopropane be di main product, no be 1-bromopropane.

questions.q: Ethyne (C₂H₂) has the structure H-C≡C-H, with a triple bond between the two carbon atoms. How many sigma (σ) bonds and π (π) bonds are present in one molecule of ethyne?
questions.e: Each C-H bond is a sigma bond (2 in total), and the C-C bond has one sigma bond plus two π bonds that make up the triple bond. This gives 3 sigma bonds (2 C-H + 1 C-C) and 2 π bonds in total.
questions.p: Each C-H bond na sigma bond (2 altogether), and di C-C bond get one sigma bond plus two π bonds wey make up di triple bond. So na 3 sigma bonds (2 C-H + 1 C-C) and 2 π bonds in total.

questions.q: Which functional group is present in all carboxylic acids and is responsible for their acidic properties?
questions.e: Carboxylic acids all contain the -COOH group. This group can release a proton (H+) from the O-H part, making the compound acidic. The other groups belong to alcohols, aldehydes and esters respectively.
questions.p: All carboxylic acid get -COOH group inside dem. Na dis group dey release H+ make the compound acidic. The other options na for alcohol, aldehyde and ester, no be acid.

questions.q: Complete oxidation of ethanol (C₂H₅OH, molar mass = 46 g/mol) with an oxidizing agent converts it fully to ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH, molar mass = 60 g/mol). If 23 g of pure ethanol is completely oxidized, what mass of ethanoic acid is produced, assuming 100% conversion?
questions.e: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. Since one mole of ethanol gives one mole of ethanoic acid, moles of acid = 0.5 mol. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.
questions.p: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. One mole ethanol dey give one mole ethanoic acid, so acid na 0.5 mol too. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.

questions.q: A housewife in a village with hard water (containing dissolved Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions) notices that ordinary soap forms a sticky scum and does not lather well when used to wash clothes. What is the chemical reason for this observation?
o: Hard water increases the pH of the soap solution, destroying the soap molecule
Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions dissolve the hydrocarbon tail of the soap molecule
Soap reacts with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions to form insoluble calcium and magnesium stearates
Soap molecules evaporate faster in hard water due to higher boiling point
questions.e: Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain fatty acid. In hard water, the soluble sodium stearate reacts with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ to form insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate, which is the scum. This scum wastes soap and prevents proper lathering.
questions.p: Soap na sodium salt of long chain fatty acid. For hard water, the soap dey react with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions to form insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate - na dat one be the scum. Dis scum dey waste soap and e no gree lather well.

questions.q: In a laboratory experiment, 1.0 mole of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is refluxed with excess ethanol in the presence of a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid as catalyst to form ethyl ethanoate (molar mass = 88 g/mol). If the esterification reaction proceeds with a 75% yield based on the ethanoic acid used, what mass of ethyl ethanoate is actually obtained?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mole of ethanoic acid reacting completely would give 1 mole (88 g) of ethyl ethanoate as the theoretical yield. Since the actual yield is 75%, mass obtained = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. This shows that esterification is a reversible reaction that rarely goes to completion.
questions.p: From the equation, 1 mole ethanoic acid go produce 1 mole (88 g) ethyl ethanoate if e complete well well - na dat be theoretical yield. Since na 75% yield dem get, mass wey dem get = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. Dis show say esterification na reversible reaction wey no dey always complete.

questions.q: During crude oil exploration and production in the Niger Delta, a large amount of a certain gas is often burnt off (flared) at the wellhead because it is not immediately collected for use. Which gas is this?
questions.e: Natural gas, which is mostly methane, comes out together with crude oil from the ground. Where there are no pipelines or plants to collect it, companies burn it off at the wellhead instead of releasing it unburnt, and this is called gas flaring.
questions.p: Natural gas wey be mostly methane dey come out together wit di crude oil from ground. If dem no get pipeline or plant to collect am, dem go just burn am for wellhead, dat na gas flaring.

questions.q: A sample of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) used for making water pipes in Lagos has a molar mass of 125000 g/mol. If the repeating unit is -CH₂-CHCl-, calculate the degree of polymerization (number of monomer units) in one molecule of the polymer. [C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5]
questions.e: The monomer unit -CH₂-CHCl- (vinyl chloride) has mass = 2(12) + 3(1) + 35.5 = 62.5 g/mol. Degree of polymerization n = total molar mass / monomer mass = 125000 / 62.5 = 2000.
questions.p: Di monomer unit -CH₂-CHCl- mass na 2(12)+3(1)+35.5 = 62.5 g/mol. To find how many units dey inside, divide total mass by monomer mass: 125000/62.5 = 2000.

questions.q: In choosing petrol components to reduce engine knocking in vehicles in Nigeria, which of the following hydrocarbons would give the best (highest) octane number, that is, the best resistance to knocking?
questions.e: Highly branched hydrocarbons burn more smoothly in an engine and resist knocking better than straight-chain ones. 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane) is highly branched, so it has a very high octane number, unlike n-heptane, n-octane and n-hexane which are straight-chain and knock more easily.
questions.p: Hydrocarbon wey get plenty branch dey burn smooth for engine and e no dey knock easily pass straight chain ones. 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane) get plenty branch so e get high octane number, but n-heptane, n-octane and n-hexane na straight chain so dem go knock pass am.

questions.q: A plastic bucket manufacturing company in Aba wants a polymer that can be melted and remoulded into new shapes several times without losing its properties. Which type of polymer should the company choose?
questions.e: Thermoplastic polymers soften on heating and can be remoulded many times because their chains are not cross-linked. Thermosetting polymers and vulcanized rubber form strong cross-links on first heating, so they cannot be melted again, and protein is a natural polymer not used for buckets.
questions.p: Thermoplastic polymer dey soft when you heat am and you fit remould am many times because di chains no tie together strong. Thermosetting polymer and vulcanized rubber go form strong cross-link wen you first heat am, so you no fit melt am again, and protein na natural polymer wey dem no dey use for bucket.

questions.q: What is the composition of an alpha particle released during the radioactive decay of a heavy nuclide?
o: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, with no electrons
questions.e: An alpha particle is identical to a helium nucleus, made up of 2 protons and 2 neutrons bound together with no electrons. This gives it a mass number of 4 and a charge of +2.
questions.p: Alpha particle be like helium nucleus, e get 2 protons and 2 neutrons, no electron dey inside. Na why e get mass number 4 and charge +2.

questions.q: A hospital in Kano stores 80 g of Phosphorus-32, which has a half-life of 14 days, for use in cancer treatment. How many grams of the isotope will remain after 42 days?
questions.e: 42 days divided by the 14-day half-life gives 3 half-lives. Starting with 80 g: after 1 half-life = 40 g, after 2 = 20 g, after 3 = 10 g remaining.
questions.p: 42 days divide by 14 days half-life give 3 half-lives. 80g reduce to 40g, then 20g, then 10g after the 3rd half-life.

questions.q: Sodium-22 (atomic number 11) undergoes positron emission to form Neon-22 (atomic number 10). In the nuclear equation Na-22 -> Ne-22 + X, what is particle X?
o: A proton, with mass number 1 and charge +1
A beta particle, with mass number 0 and charge -1
A positron, with mass number 0 and charge +1
A neutron, with mass number 1 and charge 0
questions.e: The mass number stays the same (22 to 22) but the atomic number drops by 1 (11 to 10), which matches emission of a positron (mass number 0, charge +1). This balances both mass and charge in the equation.
questions.p: Mass number no change (22 to 22) but atomic number drop by 1 (11 to 10). Na positron get mass number 0 and charge +1, e dey balance the equation well well.

questions.q: In a natural radioactive decay series, Uranium-238 (atomic number 92, mass number 238) decays through several alpha and beta emissions to finally form a stable isotope of Lead-206 (atomic number 82, mass number 206). Calculate the total number of alpha particles emitted in this series.
questions.e: Only alpha emission changes the mass number (by 4 each time); beta emission does not affect mass number. The total mass number drop is 238 - 206 = 32, so the number of alpha particles is 32 divided by 4, which equals 8.
questions.p: Na only alpha particle dey change mass number, beta no dey touch am. Mass number drop na 238 minus 206 wey be 32, divide am by 4 (wey each alpha dey carry) e give 8 alpha particles.
